item.title: AMD Unveils Lux Supercomputer to Propel AI-Driven Scientific Research
item.dc:creator: David Wilson
item.description: Discover how AMD's new Lux Supercomputer is set to revolutionize AI-driven scientific research, enhancing computational power and enabling groundbreaking discoveries across various fields.
item.content:encoded:
Small business owners looking to leverage cutting-edge technology for growth and innovation may find a new opportunity on the horizon. AMD, in collaboration with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) and Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE), recently unveiled the Lux supercomputer at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL). This powerful system is designed to support advanced AI and scientific research, potentially opening doors for smaller enterprises seeking to enhance their competitive edge through high-performance computing (HPC).

Ranked 14th on the TOP500 list of the world’s most powerful supercomputers, Lux is now accessible to scientific users engaged in the Genesis Mission, a DOE initiative aimed at advancing AI-driven science. The supercomputer boasts an impressive assembly of AMD EPYC processors, AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs, AMD Pensando networking, and AMD ROCm software—all constructed by HPE. According to AMD’s Senior Vice President Thomas Zacharia, “This partnership builds on a strong foundation at Oak Ridge and supports an open, sovereign AI stack with tools that can benefit researchers across the country.”

Lux aims to reshape how complex scientific challenges are tackled. The Genesis Mission’s projects include AI-assisted fusion power plant design, materials development for advanced manufacturing, and predictions of earth systems to assess water availability and forecasts in vital regions like the Tennessee Valley Authority area. These applications highlight the immense potential of Lux to facilitate discoveries in energy, materials, and environmental management, which could be vital for small businesses working in these sectors.

For small business owners operating in tech-driven industries like manufacturing, energy, or environmental consulting, access to a supercomputer like Lux may serve as a significant advantage. Businesses can harness Lux to conduct simulations, refine AI models, and analyze extensive datasets—capabilities that may be beyond the reach of typical in-house computing resources. This access allows for development that aligns with industry trends, potentially placing smaller companies ahead in innovation and efficiency.

However, tapping into Lux isn’t without its challenges. For many small businesses, the process of accessing such advanced technology may seem daunting. Engaging with Lux requires navigating the application processes set forth by the ORNL’s Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility (OLCF). Small business owners should consider the competitive nature of these resources; the supercomputer is primarily aimed at researchers and may cater more intensely to academic and governmental initiatives. As Georgia Tourassi, Associate Laboratory Director for Computing and Computational Sciences at ORNL noted, “By expanding the computational resources available to the scientific community, Lux will help accelerate the integration of SI, modeling and simulation, and experimental data to advance discovery.”

Additionally, small business leaders should evaluate whether their projects align with the goals of the Genesis Mission. Those exploring applications in fusion technology or environmental prediction may find Lux particularly useful, while others in disparate sectors may need to consider the relevance of high-performance computing to their operations.

The potential benefits of utilizing Lux extend beyond just immediate research capabilities. Engaging with advanced computing resources can foster connections within the scientific community and pave the way for partnerships that enhance business operations. As noted by Trish Damkroger, Senior Vice President and General Manager at HPE, “Together with Oak Ridge National Laboratory and AMD, we have delivered breakthrough engineering innovation to advance the nation’s scientific computing resources.”

As companies assess whether to pursue high-performance computing options like Lux, they must weigh the potential for transformative breakthroughs against the barriers to entry. Investing time and resources into understanding and tapping into these advanced technologies could yield significant returns in research and development, ultimately enabling smaller businesses to remain competitive in an increasingly tech-centric landscape.

For more information about utilizing the Lux supercomputer, businesses can access the ORNL Lux resource page. Engaging in a conversation with the OLCF team could help streamline the process and clarify essential considerations to make the most of this powerful computational tool.

For further details, you can view the original press release here.

item.title: How a Husband-and-Wife Building Crew Gets More Jobs Done With Temu
item.dc:creator: Small Business Editor
item.description: Sponsored Post A couple in New Hampshire have filled out their construction toolkit with gear from Temu. Now they run two jobs at once and finish some tasks in half the time.
item.content:encoded:
Sponsored Post

A couple in New Hampshire have filled out their construction toolkit with gear from Temu. Now they run two jobs at once and finish some tasks in half the time.

From her home in a small New Hampshire town, Jamie Lord can drive more than an hour to the nearest big-box store and still come home without the construction tools she needs.

Jamie, 40, and her husband, Victor Lord, run Lord Builders, a two-person construction business that builds decks, renovates homes and carries out repairs. Shops in the region rarely stock specialized equipment such as drywall stilts, bulk packs of blades and finishing tools, so Jamie buys many of them on Temu. She still buys paint and other everyday supplies at local stores.

Gradually, the couple have bought tools on Temu that save time and give each of them a full kit. They can now run two projects at once and take on more work.

“I can go to one job with all the tools that I need, and he could be at another job with all the tools that he needs,” Jamie said. “We earn extra money because we can do jobs at the same time.”

In a 2025 Ipsos survey, about one in 10 Temu shoppers worldwide said the platform had helped them start or grow a business.

Jamie and her husband, who have a son and daughter, started Lord Builders six years ago after decades in the industry. Their first job was fixing up one house, and referrals have kept them busy since. Along the way, they have added equipment.

One of those additions, a pair of drywall stilts from Temu, changed how the couple tackle ceilings. Installing strapping, the thin strips of wood that hold up drywall overhead, used to mean climbing a ladder, fastening a section, climbing down and moving the ladder a few feet. Worn on the legs, the stilts lift the wearer within reach of the ceiling. Jamie can work her way around the room without coming down. The couple finish the task in less than half the time, she said.

Jamie read the reviews for the stilts before buying and paid about a third of the price she had seen elsewhere. “They’re really well made,” she said. She also uses them to hang and sand drywall.

Hanging interior doors once needed an extra pair of hands. Then Jamie found a set of adjustable door dollies on Temu. The small wheeled stands hold a door upright so one person can roll it into place. Her husband now positions and installs doors on his own while Jamie works on other tasks.

Jamie’s workhorse is a folding aluminum work platform from Temu. Since buying it more than a year ago, she has used it hundreds of times as a cutting bench, a step for low ceilings and a shelf for paint. During an exterior renovation job, it was caught in a downpour and left outside for two nights. It showed no rust or damage when she returned.

“I’m confident it’s going to last me the next 10 years,” she said. 

With tools from Temu already on hand, Jamie and her husband say yes to more kinds of jobs. They are also ready for unexpected repairs that turn up only halfway through a project. 

“We can do it right away because I know that we have what we need to fix that,” she said.
